task: Single metadata census within exact task workspace to identify prior selected-root omissions under current capacity pressure
conclusion: The wider workspace snapshot quantifies allocations omitted by earlier selected-root censuses, but those omitted roots have no earlier full census baseline. It cannot attribute the continuing filesystem free-space change to any writer or establish unused duplicates from metadata alone. No newly eligible cleanup candidate is established.
limits: Only lstat/scandir/statvfs metadata within the exact workspace is observed; no artifact/source/archive payloads are read or hashed. Only the explicitly requested STATUS and previous small evidence JSON were read.

Symlinks are counted without traversal; errors, link counts and allocation sums are retained. Path sums can count hard-linked data more than once; regular-only observed-inode deduplication is separately reported.

A single non-atomic pass while the original fresh checker remains active. Root advised checkpoint034 preparation/capture may be concurrent; no atomic snapshot, stable-input or inactivity claim follows.
Prior selected roots permit bounded allocation comparisons only. Newly included roots have no prior baseline, and workspace totals are not filesystem-wide ownership or causality evidence.
No process was inspected, no compiler/helper invoked, no outside-workspace path inspected, and no file was deleted. Previously retired paths are not recurring cleanup options.
This assessment neither predicts complete-build peak fit nor changes the existing2,000,000,000-byte checkpoint launch floor or any formal validation gate.
